record.name: Aging and Disability Resource Center of Dane County
record.administeredBy: Dane County (Area Agency on Aging of Dane County / Dane County Department of Human Services)
record._categoriesNote: 'health-disability' is closest; the ADRC is really a cross-cutting information, referral, and benefits-counselling access point (compare wi-211 and dane-joining-forces-for-families in the shipped set).
record.summary: The first place to call in Dane County for unbiased information about aging or living with a disability. Staff help you understand options, apply for benefits, and connect to services, and are the access point for publicly funded long-term care.
record.benefit: Information and assistance, options counselling for long-term care, help applying for Medicaid/Medicare/Social Security and other benefits, disability and elder benefit specialists, and long-term-care functional eligibility assessments.

steps: Call the ADRC (Monday-Friday, 8:30 am - 4:00 pm) and speak with an Information & Assistance Specialist.
They ask about your situation and narrow down options with you.
They help with applications, referrals, or a long-term-care eligibility assessment if needed.

of._sourceText: Aging and Disability Resource Center of Dane County. Services ... available to all Dane County residents regardless of income or assets.

eligibility._note: Core Information & Assistance has no eligibility rule beyond being a Dane County resident (and, in practice, being an older adult, an adult with a disability, or their caregiver/family -- but the site frames this as WHO IT'S FOR, not a gate). This mirrors the shipped wi-211 / dane-jfff records: a referral service is worth listing precisely because it abstains.

rule._factsNote: No new facts for the core service. The specialised sub-programs DO have rules (see unencodable), several needing hasDisability and tighter age bands.
unencodable: Disability Benefit Specialists: 'individuals between the ages of 18 and 59 who have physical disabilities, developmental disabilities, mental health issues, and/or substance abuse issues' -- an 18-59 band (unexpressible) plus a disability fact.
Elder Benefit Specialist (EBS) legal program: 'senior adults (age 60+) residing in Dane County'.
Long-term care / Adult Waiver Services: functional eligibility determined by an ADRC assessment with medical documentation -- not self-reportable.
High School Transition: 'age 17 1/2 or older' with a disability.

hops: daneadrc.org -> 'What We Do' / 'ADRC Services' -- describes the service and its sub-programs; the 'free to all Dane County residents regardless of income or assets' line is stated for the core service
access.format: html-prose (no eligibility rule for the core service; sub-programs described in prose)

scopeColocated.scopeLocation: No income/asset figure -- explicitly 'regardless of income or assets'. The sub-program age bounds (18-59, 60+, 17.5+) ARE stated beside each sub-program, so where there are figures they are colocated. scopeColocated = n/a for the core, 'yes' for the sub-programs.

cost.notes: 1 fetch + 1 search. The 'regardless of income or assets' line was in the search summary; confirmed the service description on the fetched page (the exact phrase was on a related daneadrc page, noted as such).

surprises: One 'record' actually contains ~five programs with five different rules (core I&A, DBS, EBS, LTC waiver, HS transition). The unit-of-work question from pipeline-principles.md §1 ('a program, not an excerpt') gets slippery here: is the ADRC one program or a portfolio? The pilot schema assumes one id = one rule.
